name: Vincent Farah
life: “My boy and I used to draw animals on the fogged windows before dawn.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Harbour Bakery, where Vincent buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: My son painted a whale on the lid. It's the only thing he drew before his hand operation.
appearance: Vincent has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for a blunt cut just below the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Vincent looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Vincent is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Vincent asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To bring the whale lid home for the boy to see.
family: Bailey Moran is Vincent’s older cousin. Vincent leaves the first voice message. Bailey calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A doctor moves away*, Bailey says, “I have no claim on her evenings and want an introduction to the person who will read what she wrote about me.”
connections: Bianca Cole. They make sure the whale lid goes into the correct forwarding bag.
